dimension.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
dimension.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.

candidates.title: Designing Human-AI Collaboration to Support Learning in Counterspeech Writing
candidates.why: CounterQuill converts the user’s earlier reflections into a draft already occupying the writing artifact, then exposes ordinary add, edit, and delete operations on that content. This is the cleanest evidence of all three defining properties: a non-empty starting state, generated material in its final working location, and direct revision without an intervening acceptance step.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It edges out Synergi because the evidence explicitly names the in-place editing operations, whereas Synergi only says that users can iterate and customize the generated structure.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system pre-populates the working artifact with generated content that occupies its final position, and the user's task begins from that filled state.
candidates.structural_signature: Generated material is written into the artifact's own slots before the user acts, so the artifact is non-empty at first contact. Edit affordances operate on the material in place — the same handles the user would have for their own content — and there is no separate accept step gating it into the artifact. The generated portion may be marked (highlighted as adaptable, listed as alternatives) but it is already committed.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The ordering favors structural fidelity plus coverage across prose, hierarchical sensemaking, and executable pipelines. Readers should be cautious that each pick rests on a single quoted passage: CounterQuill provides strong evidence of concrete edit operations, but Synergi and ChainBuddy do not enumerate their UI controls or explicitly rule out a separate acceptance gate. Their wording strongly implies direct work on the generated artifact, but that part of the structural signature is less fully documented than it is for CounterQuill.

candidates.title: Beyond Text Generation: Supporting Writers with Continuous Automatic Text Summaries
candidates.why: This is the most complete match to the structural signature: every paragraph in one continuous text becomes a persistent card, and reorder, delete, and merge operations are explicitly scoped to those cards.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 4266 because the evidence establishes both a one-to-one partition and concrete unit-level operations, while rid 4266 establishes typed blocks but does not enumerate their handles.
candidates.pattern_summary: A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object.
candidates.structural_signature: A single artifact is divided into a set of non-overlapping parts, each given an identity (a name, a type label, a card, a row). Each part carries its own handles, so the artifact has as many operation targets as it has parts, all simultaneously present. Segmentation may be automatic or user-adjusted, but the resulting units persist as the unit of interaction rather than dissolving back into the whole.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed substantially from the consensus by promoting rid 13462 from sixth to first and excluding consensus leader rid 13585. The +0.37 adjustment for rid 13462 reflects its unusually complete evidence for the structural signature: exhaustive paragraph-to-card mapping plus explicit per-unit operations. Rid 13585 has a powerful object-oriented framework and operation set, but its quote does not establish that the cells partition one continuous artifact into non-overlapping parts. Evidence should still be treated cautiously: none of the selected quotes supplies outcome evidence; rid 4266 does not explicitly list block-level controls; and rid 16862 does not prove that its goal and intent components are non-overlapping.

candidates.title: I Want It That Way: Enabling Interactive Decision Support Using Large Language Models and Constraint Programming
candidates.why: This is the cleanest complete instance: the system begins with a time suggestion, the user evaluates that concrete proposal, and a newly expressed preference is used to improve it in the next iteration.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Metaphorian because the evidence explicitly shows every stage of the proposal–critique–revision loop, whereas Metaphorian leaves the initial system proposal implicit.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system opens with a concrete proposal rather than an empty field; the user reacts to it; the reaction becomes an input that yields a revised version of the same artifact.
candidates.structural_signature: A cycle in the control graph in which the previous output is carried into the next call together with the user's critique. Artifact identity persists across iterations — the next state is an edit of the current one, not an independent draw — so the state at round n depends on rounds 1 through n-1.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding second-ranked Code Shaping (rid 3895) and promoting Smartboard (rid 11931). Code Shaping has an interesting critique channel, but its quote does not establish that the current code is carried forward; that uncertainty cuts directly against the structural signature. Smartboard supplies unusually explicit evidence of that carryover. No selected score differs from its consensus by more than 0.3. Readers should still distrust some missing interaction detail: Metaphorian does not explicitly show the initial proposal, Smartboard does not establish the opening proposal or repeated rounds, and none of the supplied excerpts reports outcome improvements.

candidates.title: DirectGPT: A Direct Manipulation Interface to Interact with Large Language Models
candidates.why: Selecting an addressable object before prompting explicitly confines the otherwise ordinary generative operation to that object, directly realizing designation followed by a bounded write.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over PromptPaint because the evidence explicitly says selection forces the prompt to affect only the designated object, making the write boundary less inferential.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user designates a sub-extent of the artifact and the generative operation applies to exactly that extent.
candidates.structural_signature: The artifact admits addressing of proper sub-extents (a text selection, a painted mask, a stroke set, a pane, a spatial region). A designation act records one such extent as the current scope; the operation's write set is bounded by it and the complement is held fixed; the result is composited back into the original at the marked position. The scope is re-designatable and the operation is otherwise the same regardless of which extent is chosen.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding second-ranked SQUIRE and promoting Wordcraft. SQUIRE strongly establishes a bounded write set and protected complement, but the supplied abstract does not show the required designation act or even identify the scoping representation; it therefore demonstrates the guarantee better than the full interaction structure. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any inference that unselected content is technically guaranteed unchanged in PromptPaint or Wordcraft: both excerpts establish localized application, but neither explicitly documents complement preservation or compositing. The DirectGPT evidence is unusually exact, though it too is a figure caption rather than a full mechanism description.

candidates.title: DataWink: Reusing and Adapting SVG-Based Visualization Examples with Large Multimodal Models
candidates.why: The clearest structural match: the model produces a functional visualization generator with named inputs for datasets, palettes, and chart configurations, so rebinding parameters yields a family of rendered visualizations.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: DataWink ranks above Keyframer because its evidence explicitly establishes parameterized, regeneration-free reuse, not merely editable code followed by rendering.
candidates.pattern_summary: The model's output is not the artifact the user wanted but a generator of it: code, a hierarchical program, or a parameterized template that must be executed or instantiated to yield the artifact.
candidates.structural_signature: Pipeline: prompt → program/template → execution → artifact. The program is a first-class, addressable object with named parts (functions, operators, parameters) and it persists after the artifact is rendered, so re-execution under different bindings is available without re-invoking the model. Diagnostic: changing an argument changes the artifact with no new generation call. Transplants to any output medium with an executable description language — layout, geometry, music, documents.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting Keyframer from fourth to second and placing InstructPipe outside the final three. Keyframer's quote demonstrates more of the structural signature—intermediate code, execution into a distinct artifact, and direct edits—while InstructPipe is weakened by artifact ambiguity: its generated pipeline may itself be the user's intended output. The evidence for the CAD selection does not explicitly demonstrate persistence, editing, or parameter rebinding, and Keyframer likewise does not prove argument-only variation without a new model call. Even DataWink's quote does not directly state persistence or user editing, although its functional generator and named parameters provide the strongest evidence of reusable execution.

candidates.title: Rewriting Video: Text-Driven Reauthoring of Video Footage
candidates.why: The system explicitly reverse-engineers finished video into an editable text prompt, reconstructing a source-like generator that becomes the object of reauthoring rather than asking users to manipulate footage directly.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Unlike DataWink, whose excerpt establishes rich recovery but not user manipulation, this evidence explicitly identifies the recovered representation as editable.
candidates.pattern_summary: A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates.
candidates.structural_signature: An ingestion step takes a rendered or compiled artifact and emits a structured representation of it (typed nodes, fields, layers, specs); that representation is bound to the editing surface, and changes to it re-render the artifact. The recovery is inverse to the artifact's own production pipeline, and the representation is richer than the surface it was derived from.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by selecting rid 196 over third-ranked rid 4497. LogoMotion concretely recovers augmented HTML from a finished PDF, but its supplied evidence never shows that users manipulate that representation; the terrain evidence explicitly connects inverse recovery to user editing and therefore better satisfies the structural signature. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust claims about the complete re-render loop: none of the excerpts directly documents how a structural edit regenerates the final artifact. DataWink’s user-facing editability is inferred from its reuse-and-adaptation framing, and the video exemplar does not specify the prompt-to-video update interaction.

candidates.title: VISAR: A Human-AI Argumentative Writing Assistant with Visual Programming and Rapid Draft Prototyping
candidates.why: VISAR is the clearest canonical exemplar: a text editor and visual canvas concurrently expose the same argumentative outline, both permit editing, and the system explicitly synchronizes changes between them.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It edges out GUI DE because its linguistic and spatial views are more genuinely distinct peer representations of a complex artifact, making the pattern’s broader design value especially legible.
candidates.pattern_summary: Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others.
candidates.structural_signature: A shared model backs multiple concurrently displayed representations; each representation has write access to the model; a propagation step updates the sibling representations after any write. The loop is closed — starting in representation A, converting to B, and editing B returns a valid state in A.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the consensus top three; I found no structural reason to reorder them. All three quotes explicitly establish peer editable representations and bidirectional propagation, while the next candidate, CrossLit, leaves the visual-to-text side somewhat less explicit. The scores therefore retain the consensus means without adjustments. Readers should distrust any inference about measured user impact, conflict resolution, round-trip fidelity, or implementation through a literal shared model: the supplied evidence establishes interface behavior but reports no outcome results and does not describe reconciliation internals.

candidates.title: Charagraph: Interactive Generation of Charts for Realtime Annotation of Data-Rich Paragraphs
candidates.why: Charagraph directly matches the structural signature: text annotations and a chart are simultaneously interactive representations, and modifications made in either are reflected in the other.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above CrossLit because its evidence explicitly states that both representations are interactive and that propagation operates in both directions, whereas CrossLit’s visual-to-text editability is less fully specified.
candidates.pattern_summary: Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others.
candidates.structural_signature: A shared model backs multiple concurrently displayed representations; each representation has write access to the model; a propagation step updates the sibling representations after any write. The loop is closed — starting in representation A, converting to B, and editing B returns a valid state in A.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the consensus top three; I found no structural reason to reorder them. All three quotes explicitly establish peer editable representations and bidirectional propagation, while the next candidate, CrossLit, leaves the visual-to-text side somewhat less explicit. The scores therefore retain the consensus means without adjustments. Readers should distrust any inference about measured user impact, conflict resolution, round-trip fidelity, or implementation through a literal shared model: the supplied evidence establishes interface behavior but reports no outcome results and does not describe reconciliation internals.

candidates.title: DesignTrace: Exploring, Iterating and Tracking Design Alternatives with GenAI
candidates.why: DesignTrace is the clearest structural match: manual typing, suggested tags, and image-based extraction are concurrently available routes into the identical attribute slot. Because all three routes share one schema, the artifact can mix contributions freely and remains fully operable without generation.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Synthetic Conversation because the evidence names the exact input routes and explicitly shows three-way convergence on one attribute representation, rather than merely showing generated and user-added items sharing a collection.
candidates.pattern_summary: Alongside the generative route, the interface keeps a route by which the user authors the same material directly: a free-text field, editable nodes, a custom operation, a user-added prompt.
candidates.structural_signature: Two input routes converge on the same artifact slot — one generated, one hand-authored — with no mode switch between them, and the artifact can record contributions from both. Removing the generator leaves the interface still operable for that slot; the slot's schema is identical whichever route filled it.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection preserves the consensus top three, but the scores reflect a structural-signature review rather than mechanically copying the means. MindTrellis was reduced from 4.45 to 4.3 because its abstract establishes mixed-source convergence but omits the concrete user input gesture, schema details, and evidence that no mode switch is required. That omission is the main point readers should distrust. Synthetic Conversation is strong at the collection level, although the quote does not independently prove the generated and manual routes are simultaneously visible. DesignTrace has the most complete supplied evidence; even there, the quote establishes a shared attribute slot more clearly than it establishes the absence of a mode switch. No adjustment exceeds 0.3.

candidates.title: ScatterShot: Interactive In-context Example Curation for Text Transformation
candidates.why: Each LLM-output candidate is individually assigned through the same explicit three-way vocabulary—positive example, negative example, or excluded—making this the cleanest evidence of a fixed, repeated per-item disposition mechanism; the resulting choices also become demonstrations that shape subsequent model behavior.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over EchoLadder because its evidence enumerates a clearer closed set of mutually exclusive dispositions, whereas EchoLadder mixes dispositions with preview and undo operations.
candidates.pattern_summary: Every system-produced item arrives with the same small, closed set of actions attached to it, so the user's response to any suggestion is drawn from a uniform vocabulary.
candidates.structural_signature: Each generated item is rendered with a co-located control group whose members are identical across items and constant across the session; activating a member commits a disposition for that item alone and leaves other items untouched. The set is enumerable and closed, and there is no path for disposing of items that is not in the set.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the first two consensus choices but promoted rid 9674 above rid 14009. The departure is structural: rid 9674 describes a list of flagged items carrying acknowledge/dismiss actions, whereas rid 14009 does not establish repetition across items and allows Reject to produce more than one consequence. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still treat closure cautiously: none of the three excerpts explicitly proves that no alternative disposition path exists. ScatterShot's optional editing may sit outside its three-way classification vocabulary; EchoLadder's preview and undo are lifecycle operations rather than mutually exclusive final dispositions; and rid 9674 leaves independent state changes and exhaustiveness implicit.

candidates.title: PromptPaint: Steering Text-to-Image Generation Through Paint Medium-like Interactions
candidates.why: PromptPaint directly exposes a live parameter channel: users change guiding prompts during image generation, and those changes steer the in-flight process rather than a later run.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Interactive Debugging because the evidence explicitly shows parameters changing while generation continues, whereas the latter requires pausing execution before intervention.
candidates.pattern_summary: A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends.
candidates.structural_signature: The executing process exposes a control channel that remains live while it runs; commands on that channel (pause, substitute a parameter, resume, abort) take effect on the in-flight run rather than queueing for the next one. The system therefore holds partial state that is valid to inspect and to modify mid-execution.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus top three by replacing rid 10227 (Interactive Reasoning) with rid 3704. Hippo is compelling in subject matter and likely implements the pattern, but the supplied abstract does not show how an intervention reaches the in-flight process or how partial state is preserved; rid 3704 explicitly documents pausing an active run and sending new messages mid-run. I slightly reduced Morae from 4.85 to 4.80 because its quotation does not explicitly state that the same run resumes under the selected choice, though that behavior is strongly implied. No adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust interface-level details not present in the quotations: PromptPaint does not explain propagation semantics, the multi-agent paper does not describe the state presentation, and Morae’s resume behavior is inferred from the pause-for-choice formulation.

candidates.title: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
candidates.why: Morae detects decision points during task execution, pauses the active UI-agent run, and hands control to the user before execution proceeds, turning autonomous action into inspectable and revisable segments.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Interactive Reasoning because Morae’s evidence specifies the pause trigger and user-choice handoff, whereas Hippo’s abstract claims interruption and steering without exposing the concrete control or state-update mechanism.
